530	## 5. Recursion
531	
532	### Probe (p5_recursion.py)
533	
534	Each case runs in a child process so that a crash is observed. `range` and
535	`sum` are the recursive transcriptions of P13 over cons cells; `eq` and
536	`repr` apply `==` and `repr` to a cons list of length n (recursion inside
537	C); `viaC` is a Python recursion whose every level passes through a C call
538	(`list(map(f, …))`).
539	
540	At the default limit (1000), every case failed with `RecursionError` at
541	n = 10⁴ and 10⁵, on every version. With `sys.setrecursionlimit(10**7)`:
542	
543	| version | range, sum: 10⁴, 10⁵ (range also 10⁶) | eq / repr: largest n | viaC: largest n | beyond those |
544	|---|---|---|---|---|
545	| 3.10.15 | **crash, signal 11** at 10⁴ | 10⁴ ok, 10⁵ crash | crash at 10⁴ | segmentation fault |
546	| 3.11.10 | ok | 10⁴ ok, 10⁵ crash | crash at 10⁴ | segmentation fault |
547	| 3.12.2 | ok | 1,497 / 1,496 | 749 | `RecursionError` |
548	| 3.12.11 | ok | 9,997 / 9,996 | 4,999 | `RecursionError` |
549	| 3.13.7 | ok | 9,998 / 9,997 | 4,999 | `RecursionError` |
550	| 3.14.6 | ok | 47,540 / 80,453 | 7,366 | `RecursionError: Stack overflow (used 16352 kB)` |
551	
552	(Largest n found by bisection in one child. At the default limit the
553	bisection gave 997 / 996 for eq / repr and 996 or 997 for viaC on every
554	version except 3.12.2, which gave 1,497 / 1,496 / 749 at both limits.)
555	
556	Points to note:
557	
558	- From 3.11, a Python-to-Python call does not use the C stack, so a pure
559	  Python recursion of depth 10⁶ works once the limit is raised. Its frames
560	  are on the heap and count towards traced memory.
561	- Recursion that passes through C is limited separately. In 3.12 and 3.13
562	  this is a fixed C recursion limit, which **changed between 3.12.2 and
563	  3.12.11** (about 1,500 to about 10,000 C levels). In 3.14 it is a check on
564	  the remaining C stack, so the depth depends on the frame sizes of the C
565	  functions involved (eq and repr differ) and on the thread's stack size,
566	  which differs between the main thread and others and between platforms.
567	- On 3.10 and 3.11 a raised limit lets deep recursion overflow the C stack
568	  and kill the process.
569	- The harness must not use `==`, `repr`, `print` or `copy.deepcopy` on a
570	  nested answer such as a cons list of length 10⁴; on 3.12 and 3.13 these
571	  raise `RecursionError` whatever the limit. Comparison and printing of
572	  answers must be iterative.
573	- Building a 10⁶-deep cons list and exiting, which frees it, did not crash
574	  on 3.11 to 3.14 (the deallocator of nested containers avoids deep C
575	  recursion). On 3.10 the build itself crashed.
576	
577	### Classification
578	
579	A `RecursionError` is an *error* in the classes of `SPECIFICATION.md`,
580	recorded verbatim. It is not *budget*: it is a limit on the depth of the
581	Python stack, not on steps, and it is raised whether or not the budget has
582	been spent. A segmentation fault is also *error*, recorded with the signal.
583	
584	The recursion limit is a flag of the configuration and must be fixed
585	before the freeze, not raised for one problem (that would be an
586	intervention, or a control declaration tailored to one stage). Two choices
587	are coherent:
588	
589	- keep the default (1000): P13a to P13d by the recursive definitions then
590	  end in *error* at n = 10⁴, which is a finding about the configuration;
591	- fix one large limit for every problem (for example 10⁷) in the pinned
592	  3.13 configuration, where pure Python recursion to 10⁶ then works and C
593	  recursion still stops with `RecursionError` rather than a crash.
594	
595	Either way the limit is listed under the configuration's flags.
596	Reformulating a definition into a loop to avoid the limit is R.
597	
598	## 6. A budget in Python's own unit
599	
600	### Probe (p6_budget.py)
601	
602	`run_with_budget(fn, B)` counts INSTRUCTION events and raises
603	`BudgetExhausted` (a `BaseException` subclass) from the callback at
604	instruction B + 1. On 3.12.2:
605	
606	```
607	[stop]
608	  endless, budget 10:      ('budget', None, 10)
609	  endless, budget 1000000: ('budget', None, 1000000)
610	  finite(100), budget 708: ('budget', None, 708)
611	  finite(100), budget 709: ('finished', 4950, 709)
612	[catch]
613	  except Exception: ('budget', None, 1000)
614	  bare except     : ('finished', 'caught by bare except', 1001)
615	  finally         : ('budget', None, 1000) cleanup ran: True
616	  sticky, except Exception: ('budget', None, 1000)
617	  sticky, bare except     : ('budget', None, 1000)
618	  sticky, finally         : ('budget', None, 1000) cleanup ran: False
619	[pause] finite(1000) pausing at 2000, 4000 and 6000 instructions, then unlimited
620	   ('paused at', 2000) ('paused at', 4000) ('paused at', 6000)
621	   ('finished', 499500, 'instructions', 7009)
622	  finite(1000) under meter.count_mon: (499500, 7009)
623	[C loop] budget 1000 around any(itertools.repeat(0)), 5 s timeout
624	  not stopped by the budget; killed by the 5 s timeout
625	[cost] finite(10**6)
626	  plain 0.022s  under budget meter 0.652s  ratio 29.3
627	```
628	
629	The same behaviour was seen on 3.12.11, 3.13.7 and 3.14.6 (with 609 and 610
630	instructions for `finite(100)` on 3.13.7 and 3.14.6).
631	
632	- **Exact.** An exception raised in an INSTRUCTION callback propagates
633	  into the monitored code before the instruction runs. A computation
634	  needing exactly 709 instructions finishes with a budget of 709 and stops
635	  with 708.
636	- **The program can catch it.** `except Exception` does not, because the
637	  exception derives from `BaseException`. A bare `except:` (or `except
638	  BaseException`) does. If the meter switches itself off as it raises, the
639	  program then runs on unmetered (`finished`, 1001). The remedy is a
640	  *sticky* budget: once exhausted, every further instruction raises again,
641	  so no handler or `finally` block can run a single instruction. The cost
642	  is that the program's `finally` clean-up does not run either; a harness
643	  that needs it to run must allow it explicitly and count it.
644	- **Stopping destroys the computation.** The exception unwinds the
645	  frames; a generator it passes through is finished. A computation stopped
646	  this way cannot be continued, so after *budget* the next stage is posed
647	  by reposing, under restart cost.
648	- **Continuation is possible with a thread.** If the callback blocks
649	  instead of raising, the computation's thread waits at exactly the budget
650	  while the harness observes, grants a new budget, and releases it. The
651	  count across three pauses (7,009) equalled the uninterrupted count. This
652	  meets `PROTOCOL.md`'s "after budget" rule (the same computation, with a
653	  new budget), at the price of running the computation in a thread: the
654	  harness uses `threading`, which must be declared in the harness, and the
655	  callback must ignore other threads' instructions and the thread's own
656	  start-up code, as the probe does.
657	- **C code is outside the budget.** An endless loop inside one C call
658	  (`any(itertools.repeat(0))`) executes no Python instruction, so no event
659	  ever fires. Signal handlers in Python also run only between instructions.
660	  Only an external limit stops it: the 60-second safety limit must kill
661	  the process from outside (a parent process or `subprocess` timeout),
662	  and the stage is classified *timeout*.
663	- **Cost.** The same as counting: 16 to 29 times slower than the plain run.
664	  For P13's budget of 10⁸ steps that is up to 10⁸ callbacks, about 4 to
665	  7 s on this machine at the observed rate of 14 to 27 million callbacks
666	  per second (3.12.2 and 3.13.7); within P13's 600 s limit, but a cost to
667	  plan for.
668	
669	### Recommended wording
670	
671	"Budget: 10⁶ Python instructions (`sys.monitoring` INSTRUCTION, sticky),
672	per stage. Stops after exactly the budget; work inside built-in functions
673	is not counted, and a computation that loops inside one built-in is stopped
674	only by the safety limit." If the pausing harness is used: "continued after
675	budget in the same computation (thread paused at the budget)".
676	
677	## Recommendations for the study
678	
679	### Unit of step
680	
681	**One CPython bytecode instruction executed in Python code**, counted by
682	`sys.monitoring` INSTRUCTION events (global, the meter's own frame
683	excluded), on the pinned version including its patch release. Do not use
684	`settrace`. Fix `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and record it. Record whether the
685	program iterates over identity-hashed sets or dicts, or uses threads, since
686	either makes the count vary between runs. State in every table that the
687	count excludes work inside built-ins, and that it is not comparable between
688	a program that uses a built-in and one that does not, so P13e and P13f are
689	reported with the built-ins they use rather than as a cost.
690	
691	### Unit of store
692	
693	Report separately:
694	
695	1. **Traced memory**, current at the stage boundary and true peak during
696	   the stage (`tracemalloc`, 1 frame, started before the stage, peak reset
697	   at the stage start), in bytes. Not a sampled maximum. Excludes allocator
698	   overhead and memory outside Python's allocators.
699	2. **Live allocator blocks** at the boundary, as a difference from the
700	   stage start (`sys.getallocatedblocks()`), as a count.
701	3. **Process maximum resident set size** (`ru_maxrss`), only if a
702	   whole-process figure is wanted, from a separate run with tracemalloc
703	   off, one process per stage, unit stated.
704	
705	These are bytes and blocks of CPython's object representation and compare
706	only within Python.
707	
708	### Unit of alternative
709	
710	None native. **An entry in the program's own structure of pending
711	alternatives**, named in each program (a stack of partial solutions, a list
712	of generators, a frontier), counted with `len()` at stage boundaries and
713	answers, with a peak only if harness code records it. Where alternatives
714	are held as suspended generators, the count of suspended generator frames
715	(`gc.get_objects()` after `gc.collect()`) at the same points. As with
716	SWI-Prolog's choicepoints, these counts get their own row and are not
717	equated with another system's alternatives.
718	
719	### Algorithmic-operation count
720	
721	**Applications of each relation the problem defines**, counted as calls of
722	the transcribing function by `sys.monitoring` PY_START events enabled
723	locally on that function's code object, with no change to the program
724	text. For P13a to P13d this is the comparable figure across systems, with
725	the closed forms of section 2 as the expected values, provided every system
726	transcribes each relation as a definition of its own and states how its
727	count maps to "one application". Report it beside the instruction count.
728	
729	### Fixed run conditions
730	
731	`python3 -B -s` (and `-E` if no environment variable is needed),
732	`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, the recursion limit fixed for the configuration and
733	recorded, tracemalloc started before the stage when store is measured, one
734	process per measured stage when `ru_maxrss` is reported, the safety limit
735	enforced from outside the process, answers compared and printed
736	iteratively.

739	
740	- **The `python:3.13` container, and Linux.** Docker was not available.
741	  The 3.13 figures are from 3.13.7 built by python-build-standalone on
742	  macOS arm64. Instruction counts are produced by the compiler and the
743	  interpreter, so the same counts are expected from the same patch release
744	  on Linux. That is reasoned, not tested. Not expected to carry over: the
745	  C-stack depths of 3.14 (stack size differs), `ru_maxrss` values and unit
746	  (KiB on Linux is documented, not checked), absolute allocator block
747	  counts, and timings.
748	- **The patch release to be pinned.** Only 3.13.7 was run from the 3.13
749	  line. The C recursion limit changed between 3.12.2 and 3.12.11, so a
750	  similar change within 3.13 cannot be ruled out.
751	- **The cause of the `settrace` failures** on 3.12+ was not found. The
752	  observed pattern is reported; the C source and the CPython issue tracker
753	  were not read.
754	- **Whether INSTRUCTION events miss any instruction.** The count agreed
755	  with `settrace` on 3.12 where both worked, and with the closed forms of
756	  the loops, but was not checked against an independent count of
757	  instructions such as a build with `LLTRACE`.
758	- **Free-threaded builds** (3.13t, 3.14t) were not run. Monitoring and
759	  tracemalloc behave differently there.
760	- **pymalloc overhead and fragmentation** were not measured: tracemalloc
761	  reports requested sizes, `ru_maxrss` the whole process, and nothing in
762	  between was looked at (`sys._debugmallocstats()` was not tried).
763	- **C-extension allocations other than `mmap`.** Only `mmap` was shown to
764	  be invisible to tracemalloc. Which standard-library modules allocate
765	  through `malloc` directly was not surveyed.
766	- **Counting comparisons or other operations inside built-ins** (by
767	  instrumented values with counting `__lt__` and `__eq__`) was not probed.
768	- **`asyncio`** (configuration *stdlib-concurrency*): how instruction
769	  counts, budgets and retained tasks behave under an event loop was not
770	  probed. Threads were looked at only as far as section 1 and the pausing
771	  budget.
772	- **CPU-time reproducibility** was not studied. Timings are as measured,
773	  and varied by about 10% between runs.

1	# Harnesses: the common contract
2	
3	*Phase 4 (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Phases"), wave 1, written against `spec-1.0`.
4	This is the part every per-system harness shares. It changes no frozen
5	file. Where the specification could not be implemented as written, or was
6	ambiguous, the reading taken here is in [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md).*
7	
8	| file | what it is |
9	|---|---|
10	| `README.md` | this contract: what every per-system harness implements, and what every program is written against |
11	| [`stages.json`](stages.json) | the structure of every problem: sub-problems, instances (sizes, orders, answer modes), and per stage its number, description, queries and caps, commit and spawn, and the problem file's line. **No constants, no valid outcomes** |
12	| [`record.schema.json`](record.schema.json) | the JSON Schema of a raw record, the same for every system |
13	| [`validate.py`](validate.py) | checks raw records against the schema and the rules below (Python 3, standard library only) |
14	| [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) | what the specification leaves open, and the reading implemented |
15	| [`examples/`](examples) | **made-up** records and a made-up stages file, written by hand to test `validate.py`. Not runs, not results |
16	| `<system>/` | one per system, written by that system's harness author: `run`, `check`, its `README.md`, `S-mechanisms.md`, `qualification/` |
17	
18	Words in this file: *must*, *never* and *only* are requirements; a
19	per-system harness that cannot meet one says so in its own `QUESTIONS.md`
20	and README.
21	
22	## 1. The first principle
23	
24	**A harness observes what the system computes. It never supplies it.**
25	
26	A harness passes stages in, collects answers through the system's
27	standard mechanism for answers, reads state for `observe()`, enforces the
28	budget and the safety limit, and writes the record. It does not, on the
29	system's or the program's behalf:
30	
31	- suspend a computation, or wait for information;
32	- search, backtrack, or enumerate values;
33	- schedule, interleave or arbitrate between computations, or run
34	  computations concurrently itself (`PROTOCOL.md`: concurrency is a
35	  mechanism of the configuration);
36	- propagate constraints, or simplify, reconstruct, complete or combine
37	  answers;
38	- combine stages, work out the net information of a reposed run, or skip
39	  a replayed stage;
40	- order, choose, retry or re-pose goals on its own.
41	
42	Where a configuration lacks a mechanism, the harness does not make up for
43	it. The program must, as S code counted against that configuration, or
44	the problem is *not expressible* there. Everything a harness does beyond
45	passing stages in, collecting answers and reading state is listed in its
46	README as a possible confound, and copied into each record's
47	`run.confounds`.
48	
49	## 2. Terms
50	
51	| term | meaning |
52	|---|---|
53	| **instance** | one thing a harness runs: a sub-problem at one size, in one arrival or spawn order, in one answer mode. Its id comes from `stages.json` (`P01a`, `P02b.R2R1R3`, `P12c.n16.any`, `P13d.n10000`, `P16a.n1000.interleaved`). A sub-problem with one instance has the sub-problem's own id |
54	| **run** | one invocation of `harnesses/<system>/run`: one configuration, one instance, one mode, every stage of the instance in order. It writes one raw record |
55	| **stage** | as the problem file numbers it (`stages.json` gives the line). Stage k's information is held by the program, never by the harness |
56	| **computation** | `main`, the instance's one computation (or its top level); or a computation started with `spawn()` (P09a, P09b, P16b), named as `stages.json` names it |
57	| **attempt** | one try at a stage under the safety limit. A stage has one attempt, or two when the first was stopped by the safety limit and the problem allows a rerun |
58	| **query** | one call of `answers(cap)` on one computation at the end of a stage. Each stage of `stages.json` lists its queries with their caps |
59	
60	The query of a stage is always about all the information of stages 1 to k
61	(`SPECIFICATION.md`, "Stages and monotonicity"), over the sub-problem's
62	unknowns. `stages.json` lists those unknowns by name; their values are
63	for the classifiers.
64	
65	## 3. How a run is driven
66	
67	    harnesses/<system>/run CONFIGURATION PROBLEM SUBPROBLEM MODE PROGRAM OUTDIR
68	
69	| argument | value |
70	|---|---|
71	| CONFIGURATION | a configuration of `systems/<system>/README.md`, by its name there (`absys-depth-first`, `plain`, `core`, `x1sim`, ...) |
72	| PROBLEM | `P01` … `P16` |
73	| SUBPROBLEM | an **instance id** from `stages.json`, which for a sub-problem with one instance is the sub-problem id (`P07c`), and otherwise names its parameters (`P12a.n8.all`). See `QUESTIONS.md`, Q2 |
74	| MODE | `behaviour`, `cost` or `storage` (section 8) |
75	| PROGRAM | the program's path, relative to the repository root |
76	| OUTDIR | where the raw record is written: `results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/` (section 10) |
77	
78	Exit status: **0** when a valid record was written, whatever the run's
79	outcome (an *error*, *budget* or *timeout* stage is a result, not a
80	failure of the harness); **2** for a usage error (unknown configuration,
81	instance or mode; a mode the systems file does not allow for that
82	configuration, such as `cost` for *x1sim*), with no record written;
83	**3** when the harness itself failed and could not write a valid record.
84	A harness fault that still allows a record is written into
85	`harness_faults` and exits 0.
86	
87	**The harness runs inside that system's pinned Linux image**
88	(`sandbox/README.md`, `PINS.md`): `cp-systems:spec-1.0` (Absys, ALGOL 60,
89	x1sim), the pinned `swipl:11.0.1` image, the pinned `python:3.13.7`
90	image. It assumes nothing of the host. It needs only what the image has,
91	plus the repository mounted at a path it is given or finds from its own
92	location. It records the system build it ran (section 9). The launcher
93	outside the container (whatever starts it) is not part of the harness and
94	may not change what it does; it may pass the image digest in, by an
95	environment variable the system harness names, since the harness cannot
96	always read it from inside.
97	
98	What `run` does, in this order, and nothing else:
99	
100	1. Read `harnesses/stages.json`; find the instance; take its stages, its
101	   queries and caps, its commit and spawn stages, and its limits (a
102	   problem's `limits`, else `default_limits`).
103	2. Check the program with nothing but reading its bytes (SHA-256) and,
104	   where the systems file needs it, the constants input (section 11).
105	3. For k = 1 … K: **pose** stage k (section 4); for each spawned
106	   computation of the stage, **spawn** it; for each query of the stage,
107	   **answers(cap)**; then **observe()** and **print()**; then record the
108	   attempt. Apply the safety limit (section 7); after a stop, rerun once
109	   where allowed.
110	4. Write the record, then validate it with `validate.py`. A record that
111	   does not validate is a harness fault (exit 3), kept beside the output
112	   under the name `<run_id>.INVALID.json`, never silently dropped.
113	
114	`run` never decides, from what a stage returned, to pose a different
115	stage, to skip one, or to stop early. The only things that change how the
116	next stage is posed are the ones `PROTOCOL.md` names: *budget*, *error*,
117	and (`QUESTIONS.md`, Q7) *timeout*. P13's rule that larger n are not run
118	after a limit stop is applied by whoever runs the batch, across runs, not
119	by `run` (Q10).
120	
121	## 4. The operations
122	
123	These are `PROTOCOL.md`'s, made concrete. A per-system harness implements
124	exactly these and nothing that orders, chooses or re-poses goals on its
125	own.
126	
127	### pose(stage)
128	
129	Gives the system the information of stage k, in one of two ways, chosen
130	by the configuration's systems file ("The same computation"), never by
131	the harness from results:
132	
133	- **incremental**: stage k is received into the computation that holds
134	  stages 1 to k−1 (an Absys session, a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, a
135	  Python or ALGOL 60 program that reads each stage from its input as it
136	  arrives). Recorded `posed.how = "incremental"`.
137	- **reposed**: a new computation is started, and stages 1 to k are
138	  replayed into it **in order, every one of them, replacements and
139	  withdrawals included** (P10, P15d). The program carries them out. The
140	  harness never works out the net information itself, never drops a
141	  stage that a later one replaced or withdrew, and never merges stages.
142	  Recorded `posed.how = "reposed"`, `posed.replayed = [1, …, k−1]`.
143	
144	Stage 1 is always `fresh`. What the harness gives the program is only:
145	which stage to pose (k), for a reposed run the list of stages to replay
146	(1 … k−1) and any replayed commitments (below), and the instance's
147	parameters (n, order, answer mode, as `stages.json` gives them). The
148	program holds the stage information. The harness never passes a constant
149	of a problem.
150	
151	**No anticipation** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5): the
152	harness tells the program about stage k only when stage k is posed, and
153	never tells it how many stages follow.
154	
155	### spawn(computation)
156	
157	P09a, P09b and P16b. Starts a separate computation **in the same
158	instance of the system**, sharing one database, never in a separate
159	operating system process (`PROTOCOL.md`). `stages.json` lists the
160	computations a stage spawns (`spawns`) and, for P09a, the order
161	(`spawn_order`).
162	
163	- Where the configuration can run computations side by side, `spawn`
164	  returns at once (`side_by_side: true`).
165	- Where it cannot, the first runs to its end or its budget, and then the
166	  next (`side_by_side: false`).
167	- Each spawned computation has its own budget and its own execution
168	  state, recorded separately.
169	- P16b only: where the configuration does not allow separate
170	  computations to share unknowns, the four contributions are posed as one
171	  conjunction in `main` (`spawn_fallback`), with `fallback_queries`, and
172	  that is recorded. Which configurations allow it is the systems file's
173	  and the system harness's statement, not the harness's judgement on a
174	  run.
175	
176	The harness may use the configuration's own mechanism for starting a
177	computation (an engine, a thread, a program's own spawn), as the program
178	asks for it. It may not interleave computations itself.
179	
180	### answers(cap)
181	
182	Collects the answers the system reports, **through its standard mechanism
183	for enumerating them** (each systems file says what it is; for Python and
184	ALGOL 60 it is the values the program prints), until the mechanism is
185	exhausted, the budget runs out, or `cap` answers have been collected.
186	`cap` is 1 for an *any one* query and 20 otherwise, as `stages.json`
187	gives it per query. The harness never asks for an answer the mechanism
188	did not offer, never filters or deduplicates answers, and never stops
189	early because the answers look complete. Each answer is recorded
190	**verbatim**, as the mechanism produced it, with `ended_by`:
191	
192	| ended_by | when |
193	|---|---|
194	| `exhausted` | the mechanism reported no more answers |
195	| `cap` | `cap` answers were collected; the mechanism was not asked again |
196	| `budget` | the budget ran out while collecting |
197	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
198	| `error` | the system stopped with an error |
199	| `no-enumeration` | the configuration has no mechanism for asking for more: the program printed what it computed for the stage and the stage ended (Python, ALGOL 60) |
200	
201	The execution state is classified **after** the call (section 5).
202	
203	### observe()
204	
205	Records the state the common observations need (`SPECIFICATION.md`,
206	"Observations common to every problem"), **verbatim**, as the system or
207	the program holds it at the end of the stage, including at the moment a
208	budget runs out: bindings held (`SPECIFICATION.md`, "reported": a binding
209	is reported if `observe()` can read it), residual relations, suspended
210	work, alternatives held. `observe.raw` is what was read, unedited;
211	`observe.bindings` splits it by unknown only where that can be done
212	mechanically. A residual counts as reported only if it is state that the
213	system or program holds and acts on later; printing the posed information
214	back is not observing it, and the harness never makes a residual up from
215	the posed information.
216	
217	### print()
218	
219	The system's own rendering of what it holds at the end of the stage (an
220	Absys assertion's printed derivations, a Prolog toplevel's bindings, the
221	program's printed values), recorded verbatim in `print`. The harness
222	never reformats it.
223	
224	### Observing must not consume the computation
225	
226	In a configuration where collecting answers or observing would end or
227	alter the computation that the next stage extends (exhausting a
228	backtracking search in a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, for instance),
229	`answers()` and `observe()` for stage k are taken on a **separate run of
230	stages 1 to k**, and the incremental computation is left as it was. The
231	record marks each such query `collected_on: "separate-run"`, and the
232	observation `taken_on: "separate-run"`, and keeps the separate run's
233	stdout, stderr and steps under `separate_run`. Its P11 effects go to the
234	observation log (section 6). In a reposed configuration every stage's run
235	is already separate, and nothing more is needed.
236	
237	## 5. Execution state
238	
239	Recorded per computation, per attempt, in the vocabulary of
240	`SPECIFICATION.md` ("Execution state"), **as far as the harness can tell
241	it mechanically**:
242	
243	| state | what the harness reads to say so |
244	|---|---|
245	| `budget` | its budget mechanism fired (Absys `--steps`, `call_with_inference_limit/3`, the `sys.monitoring` callback, `--max-steps`) |
246	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
247	| `error` | the system stopped with an error; the error is copied verbatim to `error_verbatim` |
248	| `alternatives pending` | the system's own report that a request for more answers would resume it (a nondeterministic exit, open choicepoints, hibernating derivations), or, for Python and ALGOL 60, the program's named pending structure, read by `observe()` |
249	| `suspended` | the system's own report of held work that later information may resume (suspended equations, attributed variables with goals, a blocked engine, a program's named queue) |
250	| `finished` | the system stopped and reports none of the above |
251	
252	`alternatives pending` and `suspended` may both hold. `finished` excludes
253	the others; at most one of `budget`, `timeout` and `error` holds. Where
254	the harness cannot tell mechanically, it says so (`determined: false`),
255	lists what it could tell, and gives its basis. **The harness never
256	classifies the semantic axis, the representation, the simplification or
257	the effects class**: those are the classifiers' (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Roles"),
258	from the record.
259	
260	## 6. Commitments and the effects log (P11)
261	
262	**Commitments are preserved when a run is reposed.** At a commit stage
263	(`stages.json`, `commit: true`: P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2), the system
264	selects one of its current outcomes, v, and reports it through its
265	answers mechanism (`answers(1)`). The harness keeps that answer verbatim.
266	When a later stage is reposed, the commit stage is replayed **as the
267	information x = v**, with v passed to the program verbatim as first
268	selected, and recorded in `posed.replayed_commitments`. The harness never
269	asks the system to select again, and never parses or rewrites v beyond
270	taking the answer as the system gave it. Where the system did not select
271	(one that keeps every alternative live), nothing is replayed as a
272	commitment, and that is recorded; the classifiers judge it as P11 says.
273	In P11a and P11b, which have one stage, the outcome is committed when it
274	is reported (`committed_when_reported`).
275	
276	**The effects log.** The harness provides L and emit: one stub, with the
277	same behaviour and the same log format in every system (the binding of
278	emit into each language is the system harness's).
279	
280	- `emit(m)` appends one entry, m as the program passed it, rendered as
281	  the system renders m, to the log, and returns. It does nothing else: it
282	  does not fail, defer, buffer past the end of the stage, deduplicate, or
283	  read the log. Nothing the system does can remove an entry.
284	- The log is a file of JSON lines, one entry per line, with the fields of
285	  `effect_entry` in the schema: `seq` (position, from 1, never reused),
286	  `entry`, `run_id`, `stage`, `attempt`, `during_replay_of` (the earlier
287	  stage being replayed when emit was called, in a reposed run, else
288	  null), and `log`.
289	- **One classification log per configuration and instance**, at
290	  `results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects.jsonl`,
291	  **never reset**, across every behaviour run the harness makes, reposed
292	  runs and safety reruns included. The record copies the entries this run
293	  appended into each attempt's `effects`, and the whole log after the run
294	  into `effects.log_after_run`, with `entries_before_run`.
295	- **Separate observation runs** (section 4) and **every cost and storage
296	  run** write to `<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl` in the same
297	  folder, which is not judged (Q8).
298	- Entries emitted while replaying an earlier stage carry
299	  `during_replay_of`, so that entries duplicated only by reposing can be
300	  counted separately. The harness marks when an entry was made; whether it
301	  is a duplicate, and whether it was before, at or after commitment, is
302	  for the classifiers.
303	
304	## 7. Budget and safety limit
305	
306	| | P12, P13, P16 | every other problem |
307	|---|---|---|
308	| budget | 10⁸ steps per stage and computation | 10⁶ steps per stage and computation |
309	| safety limit | 600 s per stage, **fixed, no rerun** | 60 s per stage, then **one rerun at 600 s** |
310	| source | the problem file (`stages.json`, `limits`) | `PROTOCOL.md`, "Running" |
311	
312	- **Steps** are in the systems file's unit (Absys steps, SWI-Prolog
313	  inferences, Python bytecode instructions, ALGOL 60 interpreter ticks).
314	  The budget is a classification within a system, never compared across
315	  systems. Each spawned computation has its own budget; P16b stages 2
316	  and 3 have one for the whole.
317	- **A reposed run** has a budget of its **measured restart cost plus
318	  10⁶** (10⁸ where the problem says). The restart cost is always
319	  measured, in the system's step unit, never estimated or taken from
320	  another run (Q6):
321	  - **in-run** (the default): the harness reads the system's step count
322	    at the moment stage k is first posed in the reposed run, after the
323	    replay of stages 1 to k−1. That count is the restart cost, and the
324	    stage then has 10⁶ more steps: its budget is the restart cost plus
325	    10⁶. During the replay each replayed stage has the budget it had
326	    when first posed (10⁶ each);
327	  - **separate-run**, only where the system cannot read its count at that
328	    moment: the harness first runs stages 1 to k−1 alone, posed exactly
329	    as in the replay and with no `answers()` call, and measures its
330	    steps; that is the restart cost, and the reposed run's budget is it
331	    plus 10⁶.
332	
333	  It is recorded in `steps.restart_cost`, with `restart_cost_method`
334	  (`in-run` or `separate-run`) and `restart_cost_source`. The only
335	  exception is a configuration with no step count at all (ALGOL 60
336	  x1sim, Q12), whose records have `budget_enforced: false` and
337	  `restart_cost: null`.
338	- **After budget.** If stage k ends in *budget* and the configuration can
339	  keep its computation and continue it, stage k+1 is posed into that same
340	  computation, with a new budget (`continued_after_budget: true`). Only
341	  where it cannot are stages 1 to k+1 reposed (`reason: "after-budget"`),
342	  counted under restart cost. Whether a configuration can continue is the
343	  system harness's statement, in its README.
344	- **After error.** Stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1
345	  (`reason: "after-error"`), counted under restart cost, in every
346	  configuration, incremental ones included.
347	- **After timeout.** As after error: the stopped computation cannot be
348	  continued, so stage k+1 is reposed (`reason: "after-timeout"`), Q7.
349	- **Safety limit.** It protects the harness; it is not a measurement.
350	  It covers one attempt of one stage: for an incremental stage, from
351	  posing stage k to the end of `print()`; for a reposed stage, the whole
352	  run of stages 1 to k. When it stops an attempt, the harness stops the
353	  system by the means its README gives (`safety_limit.how_stopped`),
354	  records the attempt with what it had collected, and, where the problem
355	  allows, **reruns the stage once** with the limit raised tenfold
356	  (attempt 2, `reason: "safety-rerun"`). An incremental configuration's
357	  rerun is reposed, since the stopped computation is gone. If the rerun
358	  also stops, *timeout* is final for that stage (`final-timeout`). Under
359	  a fixed limit (P12, P13, P16) the first stop is final
360	  (`fixed-limit-timeout`). **Both attempts are recorded.** Answers
361	  collected before a stop are kept and classified on the semantic axis;
362	  only the execution state is *timeout*.
363	- A run that hits the safety limit only because it is instrumented (cost
364	  or storage, where the behaviour run finished) is recorded as such; it
365	  is not evidence about the model (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Modes of running").
366	  The classifiers read that from the records of the two modes.
367	- **ALGOL 60 x1sim** has no step count, so no budget can be enforced;
368	  only the safety limit stops it, and its records say
369	  `budget_enforced: false` (Q12).
370	
371	## 8. Modes
372	
373	Each program is run in up to three modes, one run each. A run's record
374	says its mode, and each figure is taken from the mode that gives it:
375	
376	| mode | instrumentation | gives |
377	|---|---|---|
378	| **behaviour** | none beyond the harness (its budget counter included) | answers, observe(), print(), the execution state, the effects log. **The semantic result and the execution state are taken from this run** |
379	| **cost** | step counting only | steps per stage (incremental and restated), restart cost, answer latency (steps to the first answer, between answers, to the end), problem operations, repeated work where the systems file names a source, candidates examined (P12) |
380	| **storage** | the systems file's storage measurement | store vector (boundary and peak), retained alternatives (at answers, at boundaries, at budget, peak), suspended state (at boundaries and peak), P13's maximum resident set size where the systems file takes it from a separate run |
381	
382	- **A sampled measurement is never taken from the run that gives the step
383	  count or the classification.** A sampled maximum (`peak.kind =
384	  "sampled"`) may appear only in a storage record; `validate.py` rejects
385	  one in a behaviour or cost record. Exact peaks may appear in any mode
386	  whose instrumentation gives them.
387	- A field a mode does not measure is `null`, or `{}` for the store
388	  vector. Figures that a mode records incidentally (the budget counter's
389	  steps in a behaviour run) are kept, but the figure of record is the one
390	  from the mode in this table.
391	- Where two modes can be compared, their answers must agree; a
392	  disagreement is reported as a fault of the instrumentation, by the
393	  classifiers, from the records.
394	- The systems file says which modes a configuration has (x1sim:
395	  behaviour only). P13's process CPU time and maximum resident set size
396	  are recorded where the systems file says, for growth only.
397	
398	## 9. The raw record
399

450	### Rules a record must keep (checked by `validate.py`)
451	
452	Beyond the schema:
453	
454	1. The instance exists in `stages.json`, with the same problem,
455	   sub-problem and parameters, and the problem's limits; a complete run
456	   has every stage, numbered 1 … K.
457	2. Each stage's queries are those of `stages.json`, on the computations it
458	   names, with its caps; spawned computations are those it spawns, in the
459	   instance's `spawn_order` (or the P16b fallback).
460	3. No query has more answers than its cap; `ended_by: "cap"` has exactly
461	   cap answers; `ended_by` budget, timeout or error appears in the
462	   computation's state.
463	4. Stage 1 is `fresh`. A reposed stage replays exactly 1 … k−1. An
464	   incremental stage replays nothing, and is not used in a reposing
465	   configuration except to continue after budget. After an error the next
466	   stage is reposed. A `continued_after_budget` stage follows a *budget*.
467	5. A reposed stage has a measured restart cost, with its method, and
468	   its budget is that plus the problem's budget; any other stage's is the
469	   problem's budget. Only a computation with `budget_enforced: false`
470	   may have no restart cost.
471	6. A second attempt exists only after the safety limit stopped the first,
472	   under the problem's rerun limit; none under a fixed limit. A *timeout*
473	   state and a safety-limit stop go together.
474	7. `finished` stands alone; at most one of budget, timeout, error;
475	   *error* has its text; *budget* matches `budget_exhausted`.
476	8. No sampled maximum outside a storage record.
477	9. A separate run, where one is used, replays 1 … k.
478	10. P11 records have `effects`; others do not. The entries of the
479	    attempts are exactly the classification log's entries after
480	    `entries_before_run`; cost and storage runs write only to the
481	    observation log; replayed commitments are for earlier commit stages.
482	
483	```
484	python3 harnesses/validate.py results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/*.json
485	python3 harnesses/validate.py --check-stages            # checks stages.json itself
486	python3 harnesses/validate.py --stages harnesses/examples/stages-made-up.json harnesses/examples/made-up-*.json
487	```
488	
489	The last line runs on the made-up examples: three valid records (an
490	incremental run with a safety-limit rerun; a reposing run with a commit
491	and the effects log; two spawned computations in a storage run with a
492	separate observation run) and one deliberately invalid record, which it
493	rejects with six errors.

600	## 1. How a run works
601	
602	`run` is the harness process. It reads `harnesses/stages.json`, checks the
603	program by reading its bytes, and starts the program in **its own
604	interpreter process**:
605	
606	    /usr/local/bin/python3 -B -s -P harnesses/python/runtime.py FD_IN FD_OUT
607	
608	with the environment cleared to `PATH`, `HOME` and **`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`**,
609	standard input `/dev/null`, and standard output and standard error going to
610	files that `run` reads at stage boundaries. `-B` writes no `.pyc` files,
611	`-s` ignores user site-packages, `-P` keeps the runtime's directory off
612	`sys.path`. No other interpreter flag is set; the recursion limit is
613	CPython's default, 1000 (QUESTIONS.md, Q1).
614	
615	`runtime.py` compiles the program's text, as `run` sends it with the
616	constants block's lines emptied (it never reads the file), makes a fresh module `__main__` for it
617	(`__file__` the program's path, `sys.argv = [path]`, the program's directory
618	first on `sys.path`, as `python3 PROGRAM` would), puts the name **`cp`** in
619	its globals, switches on the step meter, and `exec`s it in the process's
620	main thread. `run` and the runtime talk over two pipes (marshal frames). The
621	runtime never runs program code of its own accord: the program runs from
622	its first line, and receives a stage only when it calls `cp.stage()`.
623	
624	For stage k, `run` does, in this order:
625	
626	1. **pose**: tells the runtime stage k (and, in a reposed run, first replays
627	   stages 1 … k−1 the same way, one at a time, each waiting for the program
628	   to finish it);
629	2. waits for **main's part of the stage to end**: the program calls
630	   `cp.stage()` again (asking for the next stage), or its module ends
631	   (normally, by `SystemExit`, or by an uncaught exception), or its budget
632	   runs out (its thread is paused), or it is quiescent (section 6);
633	3. **spawn**s each computation the stage spawns (`stages.json`), in the
634	   instance's `spawn_order`, and waits for each to end its part (section 5);
635	4. **answers**: the answers each computation reported through `cp.answer()`
636	   while stage k was posed, up to the query's cap;
637	5. **observe()**: the runtime reads the objects the program registered
638	   (section 3) and the mode's measurements;
639	6. **print()**: what the program wrote to standard output while stage k was
640	   posed (after any replay), verbatim.
641	
642	The safety limit covers 1–6 for an incremental stage and the whole run of
643	1 … k (replay included) for a reposed one (common contract, Q13). After the
644	last stage `run` tells the program there are no more stages (`cp.stage()`
645	returns `None`), gives the process 5 s to exit, kills it otherwise
646	(recorded in the attempt's notes), validates the record with
647	`harnesses/validate.py`, and exits 0; an invalid record is kept as
648	`<run_id>.INVALID.json` and `run` exits 3. Usage errors (unknown
649	configuration, mode or instance, a missing program, a program without a
650	valid `CP-POSING` line) exit 2 with no record.
651	
652	Environment variables `run` reads, all optional: `CP_IMAGE_DIGEST` (the
653	launcher passes the image digest; recorded in `system_build.image`, else
654	null), `CP_PURPOSE` (`primary`, the default, `variant` or `qualification`),
655	`CP_VARIANT` (the hidden variant's id), and `CP_STAGES` (a stages file other
656	than `harnesses/stages.json`, used only by the qualification's made-up
657	problems and recorded in the record's notes).

659	## 2. The configurations
660	
661	From `systems/python/README.md`. All three have every mode (`PINS.md`).
662	
663	| configuration | what a program may use | spawn() | posing |
664	|---|---|---|---|
665	| **core** | the language, its built-in functions and types, and `cp`; no imports. Any other standard-library module it imports is an external mechanism, to be listed | one after another (`side_by_side: false`) | incremental or reposed, as the program declares |
666	| **stdlib-concurrency** | core, plus `threading`, `queue` and `asyncio` | side by side (`side_by_side: true`) | as declared |
667	| **extended** | core, plus the S mechanisms listed in [`S-mechanisms.md`](S-mechanisms.md): the package `S` (`S.search`, `S.suspend`, `S.propagate`, in [`S/`](S)), and nothing else beyond core | one after another | as declared |
668	
669	The configurations differ, in the harness, only in how `spawn()` runs
670	computations, and in what a program may import: `check` rejects
671	`threading`, `queue` and `asyncio` outside stdlib-concurrency, and `S`
672	outside extended. Whether extended includes stdlib-concurrency's
673	modules is QUESTIONS.md, Q2.
674	
675	**Imports of S (extended only).** In extended, and only there, the runtime
676	puts a package object named `S` in `sys.modules` before the program starts,
677	whose path is `harnesses/python/S`; nothing else is added to `sys.path`, and
678	no module of `S` is run until the program imports it. A program writes
679	`from S.search import search`, `from S.suspend import Var, Queue, deref`,
680	`from S.propagate import Store`, and so on. Those modules are imported by
681	the interpreter's own import system, whose instructions are counted as the
682	program's, as for any import; the instructions of `S` code are counted as
683	the program's, as it runs in the program's computation. In core and
684	stdlib-concurrency there is no `S`: `check` reports an import of it as an
685	error, and `run` gives the program's `ModuleNotFoundError`. Any other
686	import in extended is classed as in core (an external mechanism, to be
687	listed). The S mechanisms' tokens are counted once per mechanism for the
688	configuration (`S-mechanisms.md`), not in each program.
689	
690	**Posing.** `systems/python/README.md` ("The same computation") allows both
691	ways in every configuration: a program that reads each stage as it arrives
692	is one computation (**incremental**); otherwise stages 1 … k are rerun
693	(**reposed**). The harness never chooses: the program declares which, by
694	one comment line (section 3). The same program text works both ways, since
695	a reposed run gives it stages 1 … k in order through the same `cp.stage()`.
696	
697	**After budget**, every configuration **can continue**: the computation's
698	thread is paused at exactly its budget and, at the next stage, released
699	with a new budget of 10⁶ (10⁸) instructions, in the same process
700	(`continued_after_budget: true`). It then carries on with what it was doing
701	and receives stage k+1 when it next calls `cp.stage()`. (In a reposed
702	program every stage is a new process anyway.) **After an error** or a
703	**final timeout**, stage k+1 is posed by reposing 1 … k+1 in a new process
704	(`after-error`, `after-timeout`), in every configuration.
705	
706	## 3. The contract a program must meet
707	
708	A program is **one file** of Python 3.13 source in UTF-8. It is run as a
709	script: from its first line to its last, in the process's main thread.
710	
711	### 3.1 Required lines
712	
713	1. **Posing**, exactly one line, anywhere (by convention the first):
714	
715	        # CP-POSING: incremental
716	
717	   or `# CP-POSING: reposed`. Without it, `run` refuses the program (exit 2).
718	2. **Provenance** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rules 1, 2, 8), a
719	   comment block after the posing line, beginning `# PROVENANCE`, giving the
720	   author (person or agent), whether the author had seen a precursor (the
721	   absys experiments E01–E09), and the source of each idiom used (a manual,
722	   a paper, a published program).
723	3. **Constants**, if the sub-problem has any: **one marked constants
724	   block**, which the harness reads and **the program never executes**.
725	   It runs from a comment line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` to a comment
726	   line containing `CONSTANTS END`, and is divided by comment lines
727	   `# stage k` (k a stage number of the instance). Under each `# stage k`
728	   come the constants that **stage k first uses**, one assignment of a
729	   literal value (numbers, strings, `True`/`False`/`None`, and tuples,
730	   lists, dicts and sets of literals) to a plain name per statement:
731	
732	        # CONSTANTS BEGIN
733	        # stage 2
734	        A_VALUE = 3
735	        # stage 3
736	        B_VALUE = 4
737	        # CONSTANTS END
738	
739	   Nothing else goes inside, and no constant of any stage appears outside
740	   it. `run` parses the block (`constants.py`) and gives the program its
741	   text **with the block's lines emptied** (line numbers kept), so none of
742	   these assignments runs and no name in the block exists in the program.
743	   Stage k's constants reach the program **only when stage k is posed**, as
744	   the dict `s.constants` that `cp.stage()` returns with it (`{"A_VALUE":
745	   3}` at stage 2), and again with stage k whenever stage k is replayed. A
746	   constant a later stage needs again is kept by the program (it may store
747	   what it received); it is tagged once, with the first stage that uses it.
748	   The same name may appear under two stages, with each stage's own value.
749	   This makes no anticipation (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5)
750	   structural: before stage k is posed, nothing of stage k's constants is
751	   anywhere in the program's process (the qualification scans its whole
752	   memory). The program file is never read by the program's process; a
753	   program may not read files (`open`, `__file__`, `linecache`, `inspect`,
754	   ...), which `check` rejects. The verifier replaces the block's lines and
755	   nothing else, so the program must stay correct for any other values of
756	   the same shapes. A program with no block is recorded
757	   `constants.how = "none"` (right only for P04d, P04f and P08b). Sizes n,
758	   orders and answer modes are not constants: they come from `cp` (below).
759	   A block that does not parse, an entry before any `# stage k` line, or a
760	   stage the instance does not have makes `run` refuse the program (exit 2).
761	
762	### 3.2 The names `cp` gives the program
763	
764	`cp` is a global the runtime puts into the program's module before its first
765	line runs. It is never imported. Everything below is a harness call (H).
766	
767	| call | what it does |
768	|---|---|
769	| `cp.stage()` | **Receive the next stage.** Called only from the main thread. Returns a stage object `s`, or `None` when the harness has no more stages for this run (then the program should end). Calling it **ends the program's part of the current stage**: whatever the program has not done by then is not part of the stage. It blocks until the harness poses the next stage. |
770	| `s.k` | the stage number, 1 … K, as `stages.json` numbers it (the problem file's numbering, except P16d2: QUESTIONS.md of the common part, Q15) |
771	| `s.replay` | `True` when stage `s.k` is being **replayed** in a reposed run (stages 1 … k−1 before stage k); `False` when it is the stage being posed. Answers given while `s.replay` is true are not collected; a program may test it to print nothing then |
772	| `s.commitment` | for a replayed **commit stage** (P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2): the verbatim text of the answer that stage gave when it was first posed in this run, which the program must take as the information x = v; otherwise `None` |
773	| `s.constants` | a dict of the constants the block tags with stage `s.k`, by name; `{}` if none. Given with the stage when it is posed and when it is replayed, never earlier |
774	| `s.params`, `cp.params` | the instance's parameters, exactly as `stages.json` gives them: `n`, `order` (a list of strings), `answers` and `cap` (P12), `spawn_order` (P09) |
775	| `cp.answer(value)` | **Report one answer** of the computation that calls it, for the stage being posed. `value` is rendered as `print(value)` would render it (`str()`), and written with a newline to standard output, exactly as `print(value)` would, and sent to the harness. One call is one answer, however many lines it contains. `str()` of a deeply nested value recurses in C and fails with `RecursionError`, as `print` would: render such values with an iterative printer of the program's own (an output adapter, H) and pass the string |
776	| `cp.emit(m)` | P11 only: append m, rendered by `str()`, to the effects log; returns `None`; never fails, defers or deduplicates (common contract, section 6) |
777	| `cp.bindings(mapping)` | register the dict (or any mapping) that holds the program's **bindings**: unknown name → value. Read at each `observe()`, by reference: register it once, keep updating it |
778	| `cp.pending(name, obj)` | register a structure of **alternatives pending** (a stack, a queue, a frontier, a generator, a list of generators), under a name that says what an entry is. Its entries count `len(obj)`; a generator or coroutine counts 1 while suspended, 0 when finished. Any entry makes the computation's state *alternatives pending* |
779	| `cp.suspended(name, obj)` | register a structure of **waiting work** (relations or computations held until information arrives), counted the same way. Any entry makes the state *suspended* |
780	| `cp.held(name, obj)` | register anything else `observe()` should read: residual relations the program holds and acts on later, a store of values. Rendered, not counted |
781	| `cp.problem_alternatives(name, obj)` | register a structure whose entries are the problem's own alternatives (`METRICS.md`: P05's values of x still held, P12's partial sequences, P15a's interleavings); counted into `alternatives.problem_defined[name]` |
782	| `cp.relations(name=function, ...)` | name the functions that **transcribe the problem's relations**, one function per relation; in cost mode each call of each is counted (`problem_operations[name]`). For P12, a relation registered as `accept` also gives `candidates_examined` |
783	| `cp.computation(name, function)` | register the function a spawned computation runs (P09, P16b), under its name in `stages.json` (`A`, `B`, `C1` … `C4`). The harness calls `function()`, with no arguments, when it spawns it |
784	
785	Registrations made by a spawned computation's thread belong to that
786	computation; all others belong to `main`. Registering a name again
787	replaces the earlier object.
788	
789	### 3.3 Stages
790	
791	The program receives stages in a loop, and handles stage k when, and only
792	when, `cp.stage()` returns it:
793	
794	    while (s := cp.stage()) is not None:
795	        if s.k == 1:
796	            ...   # the information of stage 1
797	        elif s.k == 2:
798	            ...
799	
800	- **No anticipation.** The program is told nothing of later stages, nor how
801	  many there are; code for stage k may not depend on them (`PROTOCOL.md`,
802	  rule 5).
803	- **Replay.** In a reposed run, `cp.stage()` returns 1, 2, … k−1 with
804	  `replay` true, then k with `replay` false, in one fresh process. The
805	  program carries out **every** replayed stage, replacements and
806	  withdrawals included, and takes a replayed commit stage as x = v from
807	  `s.commitment`. An incremental program needs nothing extra for this: the
808	  harness reposes it after an error or a timeout.
809	- **Where a stage's work happens.** Only between `cp.stage()` returning k
810	  and the next call of `cp.stage()`. Steps before the first call (defining
811	  functions, registering) count in stage 1's budget and steps.
812	- **Answers** are collected for the computation that calls `cp.answer()`, if
813	  that computation has a query in the stage, up to the cap (1 for an *any
814	  one* query, 20 otherwise, from `stages.json`). Python has no mechanism for
815	  asking for more: what the program reports is all there is
816	  (`ended_by: "no-enumeration"`). Answers beyond the cap are printed but not
817	  collected (`ended_by: "cap"`, counted in the notes). Printing with
818	  `print()` is not answering: it appears in `stdout` and `print`, never in
819	  `answers`.
820	- **Ending a stage.** For `main`, by calling `cp.stage()`. For a spawned
821	  computation, by returning from its function. A thread the program starts
822	  (stdlib-concurrency) belongs to the computation that started it: its
823	  instructions count there, and its answers are that computation's. The
824	  harness does not wait for it.
825	
826	### 3.4 Spawned computations (P09a, P09b, P16b)
827	
828	After main's part of a spawning stage, the harness spawns each computation
829	in `stages.json` order (the instance's `spawn_order` for P09a), by calling
830	the function the program registered with `cp.computation()`, in a thread
831	the runtime starts in the same interpreter: one database (the program's
832	module and every object in it), never another process.
833	
834	- **core, extended**: the first runs to its end, its budget, or quiescence,
835	  then the next is started (`side_by_side: false`).
836	- **stdlib-concurrency**: all are started at once and run side by side
837	  (`side_by_side: true`); `spawn()` returns at once.
838	
839	Each has its own budget, from its start, and its own execution state,
840	steps and registrations. A name the program did not register is recorded
841	as spawned, with an undetermined state and a note. All three configurations
842	let spawned computations share unknowns (they share every object), so
843	P16b's `spawn_fallback` is never used.
844	
845	### 3.5 What observe() reads, and the execution state
846	
847	At the end of each stage (and, for a computation stopped by its budget, at
848	the moment it stopped), the runtime reads every registered object of every
849	computation of the stage and writes `observe.raw` as one line per object:
850	
851	    main.bindings = {'a': 3}
852	    main.suspended[waiting relations] = ['s = a + b']
853	    A.pending[frontier] = [(1, 2), (2, 1)]
854	
855	Each object is rendered exactly as `repr()` renders it, computed iteratively
856	for `list`, `tuple`, `dict`, `set` and `frozenset` (so deep nesting does not
857	fail), and by `repr()` itself for any other object (a `repr()` that fails is
858	a harness fault, recorded). `observe.bindings` is the bindings mapping split
859	by key (`A:x` for a spawned computation's), each value so rendered.
860	**Nothing unregistered is read**, and nothing is ever inferred from the
861	posed information: a residual the program holds but did not register is not
862	reported.
863	
864	The execution state of each computation, as far as the harness can tell:
865	
866	| state | when |
867	|---|---|
868	| `budget` | its thread was paused at exactly its budget |
869	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the process before it ended its part |
870	| `error` | an uncaught exception ended it (its traceback, as the interpreter prints it, is `error_verbatim`), or the interpreter process died (signal, exit status and stderr) |
871	| `alternatives pending` | its registered pending structures hold entries |
872	| `suspended` | its registered waiting structures hold entries, or it was quiescent (then `determined: false`: section 6) |
873	| `finished` | none of the above |
874	
875	## 4. What each mode measures
876	
877	The step meter (budget and count) runs in every mode (common QUESTIONS.md,
878	Q17); everything else only where shown.
879	
880	| mode | recorded | how |
881	|---|---|---|
882	| all | steps: `stage` (incremental cost), `restated`, `to_end`, `restart_cost`, `to_first_answer`, `between_answers`, `steps_at` per answer; alternatives and suspended at the boundary and at budget, from the registrations | `sys.monitoring` INSTRUCTION events, global, one tool; counted per computation thread; the runtime's own code and everything a thread runs inside an H call excluded |
883	| cost | `problem_operations` per registered relation, `candidates_examined` (P12) | `sys.monitoring` PY_START local events on each registered function's code object (systems file, method C) |
884	| storage | `store.quantities`: `traced_bytes` (current at the boundary, exact peak), `traced_bytes_at_window_start`, `allocated_blocks`, `allocated_blocks_at_window_start`; `alternatives_at` per answer; suspended generator frames, coroutines and async generators | `tracemalloc` (1 frame) started before the program runs, peak reset at the start of each budget window; `sys.getallocatedblocks()`; `gc.get_objects()` after `gc.collect()`, process-wide |
885	| behaviour, cost; P13 only | `cpu_time_s`, `max_rss_kb` | `resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF)` in the program's process at the end of the stage (KiB on Linux), tracemalloc off, one process per stage (P13 has one stage) |
886	
887	- **Step**: one CPython 3.13.7 bytecode instruction executed in Python code
888	  (`step_unit` in the record). Work inside built-ins is not counted.
889	- **Budget**: 10⁶ instructions per stage and computation (10⁸ for P12, P13,
890	  P16), from the start of the stage's window: the program's start for
891	  stage 1 or a new process, the posing of stage k otherwise, the release
892	  for a continued stage. A reposed stage's budget is its restart cost plus
893	  10⁶ (10⁸). When the next instruction would exceed it, the computation's
894	  thread waits inside the monitoring callback, so the count is exactly the
895	  budget and nothing in the program can catch or delay it. A loop inside
896	  one C call executes no instruction and is stopped only by the safety
897	  limit.
898	- **Restart cost**: measured in-run: main's instruction count at the moment
899	  stage k is first given to the program in a reposed run, after the replay
900	  (`restart_cost_method: "in-run"`). If the replay itself is stopped (by a
901	  replayed stage's budget, an error or the safety limit), stage k is never
902	  posed, and the restart cost is the replay's whole count (QUESTIONS.md, Q4).
903	- **Repeated work**: `null`; the systems file names only problem operations
904	  counted by the program, which `problem_operations` reports per stage.
905	- **Alternatives**: the registered pending structures' entries
906	  (`by_type` by name), never a peak (none is recorded by the harness);
907	  `held_as` is `unknown` (the classifiers decide from the program), or
908	  `none` when nothing is registered.
909	
910	## 5. Stopping a system at the safety limit
911	
912	The safety limit (60 s, rerun 600 s; 600 s fixed for P12, P13, P16) is
913	timed by `run`. When it runs out, `run` sends **SIGKILL** to the program's
914	interpreter process (`safety_limit.how_stopped`), keeps the answers it had
915	collected, and records `timeout` for every computation that had not ended
916	its part. The process is gone, so the rerun of stage k is a reposed run of
917	1 … k (stage 1: a fresh run) under the raised limit, and the next stage
918	after a final timeout is reposed (`after-timeout`).
919	
920	## 6. Quiescence
921	
922	A Python thread waiting on a lock, an event or a queue executes no
923	instruction, and would otherwise only end at the safety limit. The runtime's
924	watcher samples, every 0.1 s, the instruction counts of the computations
925	that are running their part of the stage; if **all** of them are alive and
926	none has executed an instruction over five consecutive samples (0.5 s), it
927	reports them quiescent, with each thread's innermost Python frame. The
928	harness then takes their part of the stage as ended and records them
929	`suspended`, `determined: false`, with that frame as the basis: the harness
930	cannot tell mechanically whether the thread waits for information or is
931	inside a C call that released the interpreter lock. A blocked computation
932	that later runs again is not resumed by the harness; it may be by the
933	program's other computations.
934	
935	## 7. H tokens
936	
937	The H class (`METRICS.md`, rule 13; common contract, section 11) for a
938	Python program, construct by construct:
939	
940	1. The stage loop's header, `while (s := cp.stage()) is not None:`, or any
941	   statement whose only role is to call `cp.stage()` and bind or test its
942	   result.
943	2. The tests that dispatch on the stage number (`if s.k == 1:`, `elif s.k ==
944	   2:`, the comparison, its keyword and colon; not the statements inside).
945	3. Reading `s.replay`, `s.commitment`, `s.constants[...]`, `s.params[...]`, `cp.params[...]`, and
946	   the tests on `s.replay` whose only effect is to print or answer nothing
947	   during a replay.
948	4. Every call of `cp.answer(...)`, `cp.emit(...)`, `cp.bindings(...)`,
949	   `cp.pending(...)`, `cp.suspended(...)`, `cp.held(...)`,
950	   `cp.problem_alternatives(...)`, `cp.relations(...)` and
951	   `cp.computation(...)`, with their arguments when an argument only names
952	   an object or renders one for printing.
953	5. **Output adapters** (`METRICS.md`, rule 13): code whose only effect is to
954	   render, for `cp.answer()` or `print()`, an answer already computed (an
955	   iterative printer of a nested sequence, a format string).
956	
957	Not H: what a program does with `s.commitment` beyond taking it as x = v
958	(classed by the rules), the bodies of stages and of spawned computations,
959	the definitions registered with `cp.relations` and `cp.computation`, and any
960	code that decides which result is reported. The `CP-POSING`, `PROVENANCE`,
961	`CONSTANTS BEGIN`/`END` and `# stage k` lines are comments and are not
962	tokens; the block's entries are the stages' information, classed by the
963	rules (not H), though the program never executes them.
964	
965	## 8. A complete example, for a made-up problem
966	
967	**X01a** (made up, not in the suite): *stage 1:* s = a + b; *stage 2:*
968	a = ⟨k⟩; *stage 3:* b = ⟨k⟩; the query at each stage: the values of s.
969	The program holds the relation until both values have arrived. It is
970	[`qualification/programs/x01_total.py`](qualification/programs/x01_total.py):
971	
972	```python
973	# CP-POSING: incremental
974	#
975	# PROVENANCE
976	#   author: harness-python (an agent), as the README's example; not a study program
977	#   seen a precursor (absys E01-E09): no
978	#   idioms: the Python Language Reference (assignment expressions, dict, list)
979	#
980	# Made-up problem X01a: s = a + b is stated at stage 1, a arrives at stage 2,
981	# b at stage 3; the query at each stage is the values of s.
982	
983	# CONSTANTS BEGIN
984	# stage 2
985	A_VALUE = 3
986	# stage 3
987	B_VALUE = 4
988	# CONSTANTS END
989	
990	known = {}       # the bindings the program holds: unknown name -> value
991	waiting = []     # relations held until their values arrive
992	
993	cp.bindings(known)
994	cp.suspended("waiting relations", waiting)
995	
996	
997	def plus(x, y):  # the relation s = a + b, evaluated when a and b are known
998	    return x + y
999	
1000	
1001	cp.relations(plus=plus)
1002	
1003	
1004	def decide():
1005	    for rel in list(waiting):
1006	        if rel == "s = a + b" and "a" in known and "b" in known:
1007	            known["s"] = plus(known["a"], known["b"])
1008	            waiting.remove(rel)
1009	
1010	
1011	while (s := cp.stage()) is not None:
1012	    if s.k == 1:
1013	        waiting.append("s = a + b")
1014	    elif s.k == 2:
1015	        known["a"] = s.constants["A_VALUE"]
1016	    elif s.k == 3:
1017	        known["b"] = s.constants["B_VALUE"]
1018	    decide()
1019	    if not s.replay and "s" in known:
1020	        cp.answer("s = %d" % known["s"])
1021	```
1022	
1023	What the harness records for it (from the qualification, core, behaviour):
1024	
1025	| stage | answers | state | observe.raw |
1026	|---|---|---|---|
1027	| 1 | none (`no-enumeration`) | suspended (1 waiting relation) | `main.bindings = {}` / `main.suspended[waiting relations] = ['s = a + b']` |
1028	| 2 | none | suspended | `main.bindings = {'a': 3}` / … `['s = a + b']` |
1029	| 3 | `s = 7` | finished | `main.bindings = {'a': 3, 'b': 4, 's': 7}` / … `[]` |
1030	
1031	With `# CP-POSING: reposed` the same text gives the same answers and the
1032	same observations, each stage in a new process replaying the ones before it
1033	([`x01_total_reposed.py`](qualification/programs/x01_total_reposed.py)).
1034	Its constants are delivered with stages 2 and 3; at stage 1 neither value
1035	is in the program's process. Its H constructs are the loop header, the
1036	three `s.k ==` tests, the two `s.constants[...]` reads, the `s.replay` test, and the calls `cp.bindings`, `cp.suspended`,
1037	`cp.relations` and `cp.answer` with the format string.
1038	
1039	## 9. check
1040	
1041	`harnesses/python/check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM` is the only thing a program
1042	author may run before the program is fixed. In every configuration it:
1043	
1044	1. reads the file's bytes and calls `compile(source, path, "exec",
1045	   dont_inherit=True)`, which parses and compiles and executes nothing;
1046	   syntax errors are printed verbatim as the interpreter formats them
1047	   (`traceback.format_exception_only`), and compile-time warnings
1048	   (`SyntaxWarning`) verbatim;
1049	2. reads the syntax tree (`ast.parse`) and reports, as errors: a missing or
1050	   invalid `CP-POSING` line; a malformed constants block (parsed by the same
1051	   `constants.py` as `run`): anything but assignments of literals to names,
1052	   an entry before any `# stage k` line, a name given twice for one stage;
1053	   a block constant's name used outside the block (it does not exist when
1054	   the program runs); a use of `open`, `__file__`, `__loader__`, `__spec__`,
1055	   or an import of `linecache`, `inspect`, `tokenize`, `pathlib`, `io`,
1056	   `runpy` or `importlib` (reading files or source, where every stage's
1057	   constants are); an import of `threading`,
1058	   `queue` or `asyncio` outside stdlib-concurrency; a `cp.` name that is not
1059	   in section 3.2; a program that never calls `cp.stage()`; an import of
1060	   `S` outside extended (section 2). In extended an import of `S` is
1061	   noted as an S mechanism. Other imports are listed as external mechanisms.
1062	
1063	It never imports, executes or poses anything, writes no file, and prints
1064	nothing the program would compute; the qualification shows that a checked
1065	program whose only effects are writing a file and printing a marker leaves
1066	neither. The three configurations differ only in the import rule. Errors
1067	that only a run reveals (a `NameError`, a wrong stage) cannot be found
1068	without executing, and `check` does not look for them.
1069	
1070	## 10. Confounds
1071	
1072	Everything this harness does beyond passing stages in, collecting answers
1073	and reading state. Each record copies this list into `run.confounds`.
1074	
1075	1. The runtime runs inside the program's interpreter process (the meter and
1076	   the program's objects can only be read there). It imports `marshal`,
1077	   `os`, `sys`, `threading` and `time` (and, through `threading`,
1078	   `_collections`, `_weakrefset`, `itertools`, `types`, `warnings`) before
1079	   the program starts, so a program's own import of these runs no module
1080	   code and counts no instructions.
1081	2. The program's module is `exec`'d under three runtime frames, not run as
1082	   the interpreter's own script: about three fewer frames are available
1083	   before `RecursionError` at the default limit.
1084	3. Two runtime threads (control and watcher) run beside the program in every
1085	   configuration; neither runs program code (except finalizers run by
1086	   `gc.collect()` in storage mode) and neither is counted.
1087	4. The budget counter is the step meter, in every mode, behaviour included
1088	   (common Q17); a computation is stopped at its budget by pausing its
1089	   thread inside the monitoring callback, never by an exception.
1090	5. The instructions of the program's own H call sites (loading `cp`, the
1091	   attribute, the call) are counted as the program's; those executed inside
1092	   the H calls are not, nor those of the traceback module while it formats
1093	   an uncaught exception (instruction events are switched off then if no
1094	   other computation is running; a thread the program started that is still
1095	   running is not counted meanwhile).
1096	6. Spawned computations run in threads the runtime starts; in core and
1097	   extended one after another.
1098	7. The end of a stage is read from the program (its next `cp.stage()`, its
1099	   end, its budget, its error) or from quiescence, which depends on
1100	   wall-clock sampling (section 6).
1101	8. Answers are what the program passes to `cp.answer()`, which prints them;
1102	   answers after the cap are printed but not collected.
1103	9. `observe()` reads only registered objects, rendered by an iterative
1104	   equivalent of `repr()`; the states *alternatives pending* and
1105	   *suspended* come only from registrations.
1106	10. In storage mode tracemalloc traces the runtime's own allocations during
1107	    the stage with the program's, and `gc.collect()` runs at each boundary.
1108	11. Standard output and standard error are files; the runtime flushes them
1109	    at every boundary.
1110	12. P13's CPU time and resident set are the whole interpreter process's,
1111	    runtime threads included.
1112	13. A thread a program starts with `_thread.start_new_thread` directly, not
1113	    through `threading.Thread`, is not attributed to any computation and its
1114	    instructions are not counted.
1115	14. The program is compiled from its text with the constants block's lines
1116	    emptied, and its constants are given to it as `s.constants` with their
1117	    stage; tracebacks show that text, not the file on disk.
1118
